**Kieran Kyle Culkin** (born September 30, 1982)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Santino-1) is an American actor. Known for his performances of distasteful yet sympathetic characters across stage and screen,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-2) he has received numerous accolades, including an Academy Award, a BAFTA Award, two Golden Globe Awards, and a Primetime Emmy Award.
Culkin began his career as a child actor in off-Broadway theater productions. He made his feature film debut alongside his older brother, Macaulay, in the Christmas comedy _Home Alone_ (1990). After achieving his breakthrough role as a sardonic teenager in the comedy-drama _Igby Goes Down_ (2002), Culkin took a break from the screen due to personal conflicts. He returned to film six years later by playing Wallace Wells in the action comedy _Scott Pilgrim vs. the World_ (2010). He won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for his role as a free-spirited Jewish drifter in the comedy-drama _A Real Pain_ (2024).

On television, Culkin found a career resurgence with his portrayal of Roman Roy in the HBO drama series _Succession_ (2018–2023). His voice acting work includes roles in _Solar Opposites_ (2022–2025) and _Scott Pilgrim Takes Off_ (2023). On stage, Culkin starred in the West End and Broadway productions of Kenneth Lonergan's _This Is Our Youth_. He also portrayed Richard Roma in the Broadway revival of David Mamet's _Glengarry Glen Ross_ (2025).
Kieran Kyle Culkin was born on September 30, 1982, in New York City.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Santino-1) He was the fourth of seven children born to Christopher "Kit" Culkin and Patricia Brentrup.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-hell-3) His father is a former stage actor, and his mother, a native of North Dakota, worked as a road traffic controller in Sundance, Wyoming.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Abramovitch-4) Culkin was raised Catholic with his six siblings:[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Kepnes-5) Shane, Dakota,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-6)Macaulay, Quinn, Christian, and Rory.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-hell-3) He had an older half-sister, Jennifer Adamson, from his father's previous relationship.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-7)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Santino-1) Actress Bonnie Bedelia is his paternal aunt.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-8) Culkin has German, Irish, and Norwegian ancestry.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-10)

For the first nine years of his life, Culkin and his family lived in a railroad apartment in Yorkville and struggled financially.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-hell-3)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Nilles-11) The tenement was "barely suitable for a couple," Culkin explained to _Vanity Fair_. "It was just a hallway, and there were no separating doors, except for the bathroom, which didn't have a lock. [His parents] raised seven kids in that apartment—for years! They just kept bringing babies home to this little space."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Kashner-12) Because his father served as a sacristan at the St. Joseph's Church of Yorkville, Culkin attended its Catholic school for free until the third grade.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Abramovitch-4)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Sullivan-13) He then studied theater, film and television at the [Professional Children's School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_Children's_School "Professional Children's School"), but dropped out during his senior year of high school.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Edwardes-15)

Culkin was "loved unconditionally" by his mother,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Abramovitch-4) and considers her to be his only parent.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-17) He was neglected by his father throughout his childhood and only remembers him as being a "constant, unwelcome presence" in the household.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Abramovitch-4) His mother handled all of the children's necessities while balancing night shifts as a telephone operator for a theatrical casting agency.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Abramovitch-4) According to the family's longtime talent manager, Emily Gerson Saines, his mother maintained "strong family values, like the family having a meal together, the Christmas tree, Thanksgiving. These are all important things to [Brentrup], and she instilled that in her kids."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Kashner-12) After living together for more than twenty years, Culkin's parents separated in March 1995.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-19)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Linfield-18) Brentrup was awarded sole custody of five of their seven children following a two-year, highly publicized custody battle.[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-21)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Trial-22)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Custody-20) Culkin maintained a "great" relationship with his mother, but has been estranged from his father since.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Kashner-12)

### 2003–2017: Screen hiatus and theatre work
Culkin mostly gravitated towards theatre during his hiatus, starting as a replacement for Jake Gyllenhaal in Kenneth Lonergan's West End production of _This Is Our Youth_ (2002–2003) at the Garrick Theatre.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-62) The "dream play" was the second gig that deeply affected Culkin, as he spent eight years convincing Lonergan to let him play the co-lead role of Warren Straub.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Marlow-60) For Gina Gionfriddo's _After Ashley_ (2005) at the Vineyard Theatre, he played a young man growing up in a dysfunctional family.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-63) The role won him an Obie Award for Distinguished Performance.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-64) In 2006, Culkin starred in Eric Bogosian's off-Broadway revival of _SubUrbia_,[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-65) and made his on-Broadway debut by appearing in Julia Cho's one-act play_First Tree in Antarctica_.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-24Hour06-66)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-BW06-67) He reunited with Lonergan for _The Starry Messenger_ (2009), a cosmic drama,

### 2018–present: _Succession_ and expansion
[edit]
Culkin at the screening of _A Real Pain_ during the 2024 BFI London Film Festival
From 2018 to 2023, Culkin received renewed recognition from mainstream audiences for his lead role as Roman Roy, an immature and irresponsible media executive, in the HBO black comedy-drama series _Succession_.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-82) He credits the series with solidifying his desire to be an actor.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Pi%C3%B1a-81) Culkin's performance, especially in the final season, earned critical acclaim and numerous accolades,[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-83) including the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series,[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Emmy_2023-84) the Golden Globe Award for Best Actor in a Television Series – Drama,[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-85) two [Critics' Choice Television Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critics'_Choice_Television_Awards "Critics' Choice Television Awards"),[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-86) and two Screen Actors Guild Awards.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-87)

### 2018–present: _Succession_ and expansion
Set during the COVID-19 pandemic, Culkin reunited with the _Father of the Bride_ cast for its legacy-sequel short film (2020).[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-88) He played a supporting role in Steven Soderbergh's crime thriller _No Sudden Move_ (2021),[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-89) and hosted the November 6, 2021 episode of the variety series _Saturday Night Live_; marking thirty years since his brother Macaulay anchored.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-90) In 2022, Culkin narrated the documentary miniseries _Gaming Wall Street_ and joined the adult animated sitcom _Solar Opposites_ as a recurring character.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-91)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-92) He returned to his role as Wallace Wells for the anime series _Scott Pilgrim Takes Off_ (2023).[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-93)

## Reception and artistry
Culkin has a complicated relationship with celebrity culture, having been exposed to his brother Macaulay's fame at a young age.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-116) He mistrusted mainstream media outlets following the release of _Home Alone_ because of how the press treated his family.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-117) During his parents' separation and subsequent custody battle in 1995, a 13-year-old Culkin delivered a handwritten note to the New York Supreme Court requesting to bar the media from entering the courtroom. His plea to "spare [his] family from any further embarrassment" was denied by a judge.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Sullivan-13)As of 2023, Culkin refuses to speak to _Access Hollywood_ and the _New York Post_ due to their respective coverage of his family.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Sullivan-13)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-118)

## Reception and artistry
Journalists have written about Culkin's charismatic and "chaotic" personality.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-119)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Edwardes-15)_The Daily Telegraph_'s Teo van den Broeke called him "Hollywood's most likeable rascal",[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Broeke-120) while Charlotte Edwardes of _The Guardian_ dubbed him a Manic Pixie Dream Guy.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-121) His awards acceptance speeches attracted significant media attention,[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-122)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-123) especially pertaining to an in-joke with his wife about wanting more children.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-124)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-125) Culkin has also been labeled as a style icon,[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-126) with his incorporation of accessories listed as his trademark feature.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Petrarca-127) Fashion critics noticed his recurring motif of wearing an assortment of rings, nail polishes and friendship bracelets on his right arm,[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Broeke-120) drawing comparisons to musicians Lenny Kravitz and Taylor Swift.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Petrarca-127)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-128) In March 2023,

## Reception and artistry
Culkin starred in COS' spring–summer campaign and became a brand ambassador for Zegna.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-129)[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-130) He also developed a creative partnership with Dior.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-131)[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-132)
Culkin and his wife, Jazz Charton, at the 75th Primetime Emmy Awards in 2024

## Reception and artistry
In 2005, Culkin briefly dated his _After Ashley_ co-star Anna Paquin.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-133) He was in a relationship with his _Paper Man_ co-star Emma Stone from 2009 to 2011.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-134) They remained good friends following their split and continued to work together on _Movie 43_ and _A Real Pain_.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-135) In 2012, Culkin met British advertising specialist Jazz Charton.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-136) They eloped on June 22, 2013, during a cross-country road trip in Iowa.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Kahn-137) The couple have three children together;[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-138) Culkin's _Succession_ co-star Sarah Snook is the godmother to their second child.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-139) The family resides in Greenpoint, Brooklyn.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Sullivan-13)

## Reception and artistry
Some of Culkin's hobbies are cooking,[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Kahn-137) playing retro video games,[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-140) and watching professional wrestling.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Kashner-12) His _She's All That_ co-star [Freddie Prinze Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Prinze_Jr. "Freddie Prinze Jr.") described him as an "encyclopedia" of the latter.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-141) Culkin has attended an estimated ten editions of WrestleMania, the annual flagship event held by WWE.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-142) He is also proficient in American Sign Language.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-143)

## Reception and artistry
Culkin became friends with singer Michael Jackson around the time _Home Alone_ was released.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Robinson-144) He frequently visited his residence, Neverland Ranch, with his siblings.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Robinson-144) During the 2003 television program _Living with Michael Jackson_, the singer defended his practice of inviting children into his bedroom by telling British journalist Martin Bashir that "many children," including Culkin, had slept in the same bed as him.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-145) The program triggered an investigation and Jackson was formally charged with seven counts of child molestation;[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-146) he was later acquitted in a court of law in 2005.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-147) Culkin declined to speak about his relationship with Jackson in the wake of the documentary film _Leaving Neverland_ (2019), due to its sensitive nature.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-148)

## Acting credits and awards
[edit]
Among his major competitive awards, Culkin has won an Academy Award,[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Oscar_2025-98) a BAFTA Award,[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-BAFTA_2025-99) a Primetime Emmy Award,[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-149) and two Golden Globe Awards.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-150)[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-151) He is the first performer to win the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor from a film that was not nominated in Best Picture since Christopher Plummer in 2012.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-152)

**Kieran Kyle Culkin** (born September 30, 1982)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Santino-1) is an American actor. Known for his performances of distasteful yet sympathetic characters across stage and screen,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-2) he has received numerous accolades, including an Academy Award, a BAFTA Award, two Golden Globe Awards, and a Primetime Emmy Award.
Culkin began his career as a child actor in off-Broadway theater productions. He made his feature film debut alongside his older brother, Macaulay, in the Christmas comedy _Home Alone_ (1990). After achieving his breakthrough role as a sardonic teenager in the comedy-drama _Igby Goes Down_ (2002), Culkin took a break from the screen due to personal conflicts. He returned to film six years later by playing Wallace Wells in the action comedy _Scott Pilgrim vs. the World_ (2010). He won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for his role as a free-spirited Jewish drifter in the comedy-drama _A Real Pain_ (2024).
texts.1:
On television, Culkin found a career resurgence with his portrayal of Roman Roy in the HBO drama series _Succession_ (2018–2023). His voice acting work includes roles in _Solar Opposites_ (2022–2025) and _Scott Pilgrim Takes Off_ (2023). On stage, Culkin starred in the West End and Broadway productions of Kenneth Lonergan's _This Is Our Youth_. He also portrayed Richard Roma in the Broadway revival of David Mamet's _Glengarry Glen Ross_ (2025).
Kieran Kyle Culkin was born on September 30, 1982, in New York City.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Santino-1) He was the fourth of seven children born to Christopher "Kit" Culkin and Patricia Brentrup.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-hell-3) His father is a former stage actor, and his mother, a native of North Dakota, worked as a road traffic controller in Sundance, Wyoming.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Abramovitch-4) Culkin was raised Catholic with his six siblings:[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Kepnes-5) Shane, Dakota,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-6)Macaulay, Quinn, Christian, and Rory.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-hell-3) He had an older half-sister, Jennifer Adamson, from his father's previous relationship.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-7)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Santino-1) Actress Bonnie Bedelia is his paternal aunt.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-8) Culkin has German, Irish, and Norwegian ancestry.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-10)
texts.2: For the first nine years of his life, Culkin and his family lived in a railroad apartment in Yorkville and struggled financially.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-hell-3)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Nilles-11) The tenement was "barely suitable for a couple," Culkin explained to _Vanity Fair_. "It was just a hallway, and there were no separating doors, except for the bathroom, which didn't have a lock. [His parents] raised seven kids in that apartment—for years! They just kept bringing babies home to this little space."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Kashner-12) Because his father served as a sacristan at the St. Joseph's Church of Yorkville, Culkin attended its Catholic school for free until the third grade.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Abramovitch-4)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Sullivan-13) He then studied theater, film and television at the [Professional Children's School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_Children's_School "Professional Children's School"), but dropped out during his senior year of high school.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Edwardes-15)
texts.3: Culkin was "loved unconditionally" by his mother,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Abramovitch-4) and considers her to be his only parent.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-17) He was neglected by his father throughout his childhood and only remembers him as being a "constant, unwelcome presence" in the household.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Abramovitch-4) His mother handled all of the children's necessities while balancing night shifts as a telephone operator for a theatrical casting agency.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Abramovitch-4) According to the family's longtime talent manager, Emily Gerson Saines, his mother maintained "strong family values, like the family having a meal together, the Christmas tree, Thanksgiving. These are all important things to [Brentrup], and she instilled that in her kids."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Kashner-12) After living together for more than twenty years, Culkin's parents separated in March 1995.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-19)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Linfield-18) Brentrup was awarded sole custody of five of their seven children following a two-year, highly publicized custody battle.[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-21)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Trial-22)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Custody-20) Culkin maintained a "great" relationship with his mother, but has been estranged from his father since.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Kashner-12)

His plea to "spare [his] family from any further embarrassment" was denied by a judge.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Sullivan-13)As of 2023, Culkin refuses to speak to _Access Hollywood_ and the _New York Post_ due to their respective coverage of his family.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Sullivan-13)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-118)

## Reception and artistry
Journalists have written about Culkin's charismatic and "chaotic" personality.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-119)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Edwardes-15)_The Daily Telegraph_'s Teo van den Broeke called him "Hollywood's most likeable rascal",[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Broeke-120) while Charlotte Edwardes of _The Guardian_ dubbed him a Manic Pixie Dream Guy.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-121) His awards acceptance speeches attracted significant media attention,[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-122)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-123) especially pertaining to an in-joke with his wife about wanting more children.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-124)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-125) Culkin has also been labeled as a style icon,[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-126) with his incorporation of accessories listed as his trademark feature.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Petrarca-127) Fashion critics noticed his recurring motif of wearing an assortment of rings, nail polishes and friendship bracelets on his right arm,[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Broeke-120) drawing comparisons to musicians Lenny Kravitz and Taylor Swift.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Petrarca-127)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-128) In March 2023,

## Reception and artistry
In 2005, Culkin briefly dated his _After Ashley_ co-star Anna Paquin.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-133) He was in a relationship with his _Paper Man_ co-star Emma Stone from 2009 to 2011.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-134) They remained good friends following their split and continued to work together on _Movie 43_ and _A Real Pain_.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-135) In 2012, Culkin met British advertising specialist Jazz Charton.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-136) They eloped on June 22, 2013, during a cross-country road trip in Iowa.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Kahn-137) The couple have three children together;[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-138) Culkin's _Succession_ co-star Sarah Snook is the godmother to their second child.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-139) The family resides in Greenpoint, Brooklyn.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Sullivan-13)

## Reception and artistry
Some of Culkin's hobbies are cooking,[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Kahn-137) playing retro video games,[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-140) and watching professional wrestling.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Kashner-12) His _She's All That_ co-star [Freddie Prinze Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Prinze_Jr. "Freddie Prinze Jr.") described him as an "encyclopedia" of the latter.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-141) Culkin has attended an estimated ten editions of WrestleMania, the annual flagship event held by WWE.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-142) He is also proficient in American Sign Language.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-143)

## Reception and artistry
Culkin became friends with singer Michael Jackson around the time _Home Alone_ was released.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Robinson-144) He frequently visited his residence, Neverland Ranch, with his siblings.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Robinson-144) During the 2003 television program _Living with Michael Jackson_, the singer defended his practice of inviting children into his bedroom by telling British journalist Martin Bashir that "many children," including Culkin, had slept in the same bed as him.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-145) The program triggered an investigation and Jackson was formally charged with seven counts of child molestation;[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-146) he was later acquitted in a court of law in 2005.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-147) Culkin declined to speak about his relationship with Jackson in the wake of the documentary film _Leaving Neverland_ (2019), due to its sensitive nature.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-148)

**Kieran Kyle Culkin** (born September 30, 1982)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Santino-1) is an American actor. Known for his performances of distasteful yet sympathetic characters across stage and screen,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-2) he has received numerous accolades, including an Academy Award, a BAFTA Award, two Golden Globe Awards, and a Primetime Emmy Award.
Culkin began his career as a child actor in off-Broadway theater productions. He made his feature film debut alongside his older brother, Macaulay, in the Christmas comedy _Home Alone_ (1990). After achieving his breakthrough role as a sardonic teenager in the comedy-drama _Igby Goes Down_ (2002), Culkin took a break from the screen due to personal conflicts. He returned to film six years later by playing Wallace Wells in the action comedy _Scott Pilgrim vs. the World_ (2010). He won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for his role as a free-spirited Jewish drifter in the comedy-drama _A Real Pain_ (2024).

On television, Culkin found a career resurgence with his portrayal of Roman Roy in the HBO drama series _Succession_ (2018–2023). His voice acting work includes roles in _Solar Opposites_ (2022–2025) and _Scott Pilgrim Takes Off_ (2023). On stage, Culkin starred in the West End and Broadway productions of Kenneth Lonergan's _This Is Our Youth_. He also portrayed Richard Roma in the Broadway revival of David Mamet's _Glengarry Glen Ross_ (2025).
Kieran Kyle Culkin was born on September 30, 1982, in New York City.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Santino-1) He was the fourth of seven children born to Christopher "Kit" Culkin and Patricia Brentrup.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-hell-3) His father is a former stage actor, and his mother, a native of North Dakota, worked as a road traffic controller in Sundance, Wyoming.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Abramovitch-4) Culkin was raised Catholic with his six siblings:[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Kepnes-5) Shane, Dakota,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-6)Macaulay, Quinn, Christian, and Rory.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-hell-3) He had an older half-sister, Jennifer Adamson, from his father's previous relationship.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-7)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Santino-1) Actress Bonnie Bedelia is his paternal aunt.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-8) Culkin has German, Irish, and Norwegian ancestry.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-10)

For the first nine years of his life, Culkin and his family lived in a railroad apartment in Yorkville and struggled financially.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-hell-3)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Nilles-11) The tenement was "barely suitable for a couple," Culkin explained to _Vanity Fair_. "It was just a hallway, and there were no separating doors, except for the bathroom, which didn't have a lock. [His parents] raised seven kids in that apartment—for years! They just kept bringing babies home to this little space."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Kashner-12) Because his father served as a sacristan at the St. Joseph's Church of Yorkville, Culkin attended its Catholic school for free until the third grade.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Abramovitch-4)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Sullivan-13) He then studied theater, film and television at the [Professional Children's School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_Children's_School "Professional Children's School"), but dropped out during his senior year of high school.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Edwardes-15)

Culkin was "loved unconditionally" by his mother,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Abramovitch-4) and considers her to be his only parent.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-17) He was neglected by his father throughout his childhood and only remembers him as being a "constant, unwelcome presence" in the household.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Abramovitch-4) His mother handled all of the children's necessities while balancing night shifts as a telephone operator for a theatrical casting agency.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Abramovitch-4) According to the family's longtime talent manager, Emily Gerson Saines, his mother maintained "strong family values, like the family having a meal together, the Christmas tree, Thanksgiving. These are all important things to [Brentrup], and she instilled that in her kids."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Kashner-12) After living together for more than twenty years, Culkin's parents separated in March 1995.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-19)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Linfield-18) Brentrup was awarded sole custody of five of their seven children following a two-year, highly publicized custody battle.[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-21)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Trial-22)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Custody-20) Culkin maintained a "great" relationship with his mother, but has been estranged from his father since.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Kashner-12)

### 2003–2017: Screen hiatus and theatre work
Culkin mostly gravitated towards theatre during his hiatus, starting as a replacement for Jake Gyllenhaal in Kenneth Lonergan's West End production of _This Is Our Youth_ (2002–2003) at the Garrick Theatre.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-62) The "dream play" was the second gig that deeply affected Culkin, as he spent eight years convincing Lonergan to let him play the co-lead role of Warren Straub.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Marlow-60) For Gina Gionfriddo's _After Ashley_ (2005) at the Vineyard Theatre, he played a young man growing up in a dysfunctional family.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-63) The role won him an Obie Award for Distinguished Performance.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-64) In 2006, Culkin starred in Eric Bogosian's off-Broadway revival of _SubUrbia_,[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-65) and made his on-Broadway debut by appearing in Julia Cho's one-act play_First Tree in Antarctica_.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-24Hour06-66)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-BW06-67) He reunited with Lonergan for _The Starry Messenger_ (2009), a cosmic drama,

### 2018–present: _Succession_ and expansion
[edit]
Culkin at the screening of _A Real Pain_ during the 2024 BFI London Film Festival
From 2018 to 2023, Culkin received renewed recognition from mainstream audiences for his lead role as Roman Roy, an immature and irresponsible media executive, in the HBO black comedy-drama series _Succession_.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-82) He credits the series with solidifying his desire to be an actor.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Pi%C3%B1a-81) Culkin's performance, especially in the final season, earned critical acclaim and numerous accolades,[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-83) including the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series,[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Emmy_2023-84) the Golden Globe Award for Best Actor in a Television Series – Drama,[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-85) two [Critics' Choice Television Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critics'_Choice_Television_Awards "Critics' Choice Television Awards"),[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-86) and two Screen Actors Guild Awards.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-87)

### 2018–present: _Succession_ and expansion
Set during the COVID-19 pandemic, Culkin reunited with the _Father of the Bride_ cast for its legacy-sequel short film (2020).[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-88) He played a supporting role in Steven Soderbergh's crime thriller _No Sudden Move_ (2021),[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-89) and hosted the November 6, 2021 episode of the variety series _Saturday Night Live_; marking thirty years since his brother Macaulay anchored.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-90) In 2022, Culkin narrated the documentary miniseries _Gaming Wall Street_ and joined the adult animated sitcom _Solar Opposites_ as a recurring character.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-91)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-92) He returned to his role as Wallace Wells for the anime series _Scott Pilgrim Takes Off_ (2023).[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-93)

## Reception and artistry
Culkin has a complicated relationship with celebrity culture, having been exposed to his brother Macaulay's fame at a young age.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-116) He mistrusted mainstream media outlets following the release of _Home Alone_ because of how the press treated his family.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-117) During his parents' separation and subsequent custody battle in 1995, a 13-year-old Culkin delivered a handwritten note to the New York Supreme Court requesting to bar the media from entering the courtroom. His plea to "spare [his] family from any further embarrassment" was denied by a judge.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Sullivan-13)As of 2023, Culkin refuses to speak to _Access Hollywood_ and the _New York Post_ due to their respective coverage of his family.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Sullivan-13)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-118)

## Reception and artistry
Journalists have written about Culkin's charismatic and "chaotic" personality.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-119)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Edwardes-15)_The Daily Telegraph_'s Teo van den Broeke called him "Hollywood's most likeable rascal",[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Broeke-120) while Charlotte Edwardes of _The Guardian_ dubbed him a Manic Pixie Dream Guy.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-121) His awards acceptance speeches attracted significant media attention,[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-122)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-123) especially pertaining to an in-joke with his wife about wanting more children.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-124)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-125) Culkin has also been labeled as a style icon,[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-126) with his incorporation of accessories listed as his trademark feature.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Petrarca-127) Fashion critics noticed his recurring motif of wearing an assortment of rings, nail polishes and friendship bracelets on his right arm,[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Broeke-120) drawing comparisons to musicians Lenny Kravitz and Taylor Swift.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Petrarca-127)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-128) In March 2023,

## Reception and artistry
Culkin starred in COS' spring–summer campaign and became a brand ambassador for Zegna.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-129)[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-130) He also developed a creative partnership with Dior.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-131)[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-132)
Culkin and his wife, Jazz Charton, at the 75th Primetime Emmy Awards in 2024

## Reception and artistry
In 2005, Culkin briefly dated his _After Ashley_ co-star Anna Paquin.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-133) He was in a relationship with his _Paper Man_ co-star Emma Stone from 2009 to 2011.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-134) They remained good friends following their split and continued to work together on _Movie 43_ and _A Real Pain_.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-135) In 2012, Culkin met British advertising specialist Jazz Charton.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-136) They eloped on June 22, 2013, during a cross-country road trip in Iowa.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Kahn-137) The couple have three children together;[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-138) Culkin's _Succession_ co-star Sarah Snook is the godmother to their second child.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-139) The family resides in Greenpoint, Brooklyn.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Sullivan-13)

## Reception and artistry
Some of Culkin's hobbies are cooking,[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Kahn-137) playing retro video games,[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-140) and watching professional wrestling.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Kashner-12) His _She's All That_ co-star [Freddie Prinze Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Prinze_Jr. "Freddie Prinze Jr.") described him as an "encyclopedia" of the latter.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-141) Culkin has attended an estimated ten editions of WrestleMania, the annual flagship event held by WWE.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-142) He is also proficient in American Sign Language.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-143)

## Reception and artistry
Culkin became friends with singer Michael Jackson around the time _Home Alone_ was released.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Robinson-144) He frequently visited his residence, Neverland Ranch, with his siblings.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Robinson-144) During the 2003 television program _Living with Michael Jackson_, the singer defended his practice of inviting children into his bedroom by telling British journalist Martin Bashir that "many children," including Culkin, had slept in the same bed as him.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-145) The program triggered an investigation and Jackson was formally charged with seven counts of child molestation;[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-146) he was later acquitted in a court of law in 2005.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-147) Culkin declined to speak about his relationship with Jackson in the wake of the documentary film _Leaving Neverland_ (2019), due to its sensitive nature.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-148)

## Acting credits and awards
[edit]
Among his major competitive awards, Culkin has won an Academy Award,[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-Oscar_2025-98) a BAFTA Award,[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-BAFTA_2025-99) a Primetime Emmy Award,[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-149) and two Golden Globe Awards.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-150)[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-151) He is the first performer to win the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor from a film that was not nominated in Best Picture since Christopher Plummer in 2012.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Culkin#cite_note-152)

Title: Life After Art School
Chunks: 20,21,22,23,24,25,26
## **The art world has its own version of the Hollywood dream**
### **There is no deadline for success**
The way the news media covers visual artists does not help either. The only artists who get significant press coverage are the ones who hada sudden, meteoric rise, who skyrocketed into the art world after being plucked out of anMFA program in NYC. Or, it’s articles like Forbes’ “30 under 30” as if 30 is your deadline for success.
The only artist success story article I’ve ever read that was helpful wasthis one written by “Mad Men” creator Matthew Weiner. I read this article once in a while when I feel demoralized, and it helps every time!

## **The art world has its own version of the Hollywood dream**
### **A personal connection can be everything**
Many articles conveniently don’t mention those personal connections that started an art career. From the outside, how these people get onto these lists seems completely baffling.
The truth is, many of the people in these lists are not necessarily any better or more deserving than anyone else. Many of them had a significant personal connection that gave them membership into a very exclusive club.
Once you realize how a personal connection can make a career, you’ll start to notice how common it is. Case in point:this New Yorker articlethat mentions thatRyan Trecartin‘s father, Dell Trecartin, was a childhood friend ofKen Johnson (an art critic for the New York Times).
Johnson andLinda Norden(at that time, Norden was a curator atHarvard University’s Fogg Art Museum) attended the first public screening of an early film by Ryan Trecartin at the Rhode Island School of Design. The article goes on to state that Norden “would become one of Trecartin’s most effective supporters.”

## **The art world has its own version of the Hollywood dream**
### **Most artists only show you their success, no one talks about what’s difficult**
A lot of art schools bring successful, recent alums to lecture and speak about their experiences. Schools naturally want students to have a point of reference for what’s possible, so it makes sense to bring in the alums who have experienced that success early.
However, many of these successful recent alums giving these talks don’t bother to address the less glamorous parts of being an artist, any periods of struggle prior to their success, financial difficulties.
From the outside, the process of building a career in visual arts can appear to be a piece of cake. Social media only perpetuates this, as many young artists heavily curate their feeds to appear much happier and more successful than they actually are.

## **The art world has its own version of the Hollywood dream**
### **Every artist struggles at some point!**
All of this is hugely misleading to artists at the very beginning of their career, you feel like you are the only artist in the world who is having a hard time, that everyone else is more content, more active, younger, have had success much earlier than you!
In theory, it should be inspiring to hear these successful alums who attended the same art school. More often than not though, students feel very demoralized afterwards. Every year, I hear the same comments from students afterwards:
**_“I’m so depressed.”_**
**_“I’m never going to make it.”_**
**_“I’m so behind.”_**
**_“I’m already a junior and I haven’t done anything yet!”_**
> _**“Fear not: as grim as the career of an artist may look at times, there are more ways than ever to get your work out there and make it work! I found little success when I was just looking at book publishers.**_  
>   
>   
> _**Now that I’ve started meeting local bands, interacting with small businesses, and even joining a gallery (trust me, the last place I thought my work would fit!) I’m slowly finding people who I can work with as an artist.Be honest with your artwork, and the right venue for it will come.**_  
>   
>   
> _**Don’t try to make your work fit a specific goal, but try to find a goal that fits the kind of art you enjoy. In my experience, as I let go of the assumption that I knew what I wanted to do, I’ve been having so much more fun making my work again!**_**_”_**  
>   
> Alex Rowe  
>   
> Illustrator & Children’s Book Artist

## **The art world has its own version of the Hollywood dream**
### **Every artist struggles at some point!**
> _**“Sometimes I feel embarrassed that I lived with my parents for so long, but I try to be honest about it. Jobs in the art world can be competitive and many do not pay well especially when you’re just starting out.**_  
>   
>   
> _**Since I didn’t have the pressure of making rent for several years, I was able to put a lot of time and energy into my gallery position, studio, and professional relationships, while paying off my student loans.**_  
>   
>   
> _**Creating this network of social and professional support has been enormously helpful for my artistic and financial stability as I transition into my own place in New York City.”**_  
>   
> Lauryn Welch  
>   
> Painter & Performance Artist

## **The art world has its own version of the Hollywood dream**
### **Pursue what YOU want to do, not what everyone else says you should do**
Most of the time nowadays, I practically bolt out of bed and with feverish enthusiasm on my current projects. However, I still get self-conscious from time to time about taking an alternative path as an artist.
When that happens, I remember what my former professor said to me, and I can renew my confidence in the path I chose to take.
For many years after finished myMFA degree, I was trying to fulfillsomeone else’s checklist of goals that were not my own. Since I walked away from that checklist of goals, the world is a _much_ bigger place, and I’m seeing opportunities in places I never would have considered options even just 5 years ago.

## **The art world has its own version of the Hollywood dream**
### **Consider just having an active art practice a success**
What art schools should do (which they never will) is bring in recent alums who are just barely sustaining our artistic practice. Those of us who have had little or moderate success, but who are still actively producing their artwork.
For most of us, maintaining a studio practice is a long, tedious, incremental, slow slog that isn’t so easy.
However, in my opinion, maintaining an active studio practice is in itself an achievement to be recognized. It’s no small feat to juggle jobs, paying bills, family/friends, and everything else that life throws at you while simultaneously being able to find the head space and time to create on a long term basis.
Do what it takes to keep your art practice alive, _anything_ that motivates you is valid.

For most of us, maintaining a studio practice is a long, tedious, incremental, slow slog that isn’t so easy.
However, in my opinion, maintaining an active studio practice is in itself an achievement to be recognized. It’s no small feat to juggle jobs, paying bills, family/friends, and everything else that life throws at you while simultaneously being able to find the head space and time to create on a long term basis.
Do what it takes to keep your art practice alive, _anything_ that motivates you is valid.

## **The art world has its own version of the Hollywood dream**
### **There is no deadline for success**
The way the news media covers visual artists does not help either. The only artists who get significant press coverage are the ones who hada sudden, meteoric rise, who skyrocketed into the art world after being plucked out of anMFA program in NYC. Or, it’s articles like Forbes’ “30 under 30” as if 30 is your deadline for success.
The only artist success story article I’ve ever read that was helpful wasthis one written by “Mad Men” creator Matthew Weiner. I read this article once in a while when I feel demoralized, and it helps every time!

## **The art world has its own version of the Hollywood dream**
### **A personal connection can be everything**
Many articles conveniently don’t mention those personal connections that started an art career. From the outside, how these people get onto these lists seems completely baffling.
The truth is, many of the people in these lists are not necessarily any better or more deserving than anyone else. Many of them had a significant personal connection that gave them membership into a very exclusive club.
Once you realize how a personal connection can make a career, you’ll start to notice how common it is. Case in point:this New Yorker articlethat mentions thatRyan Trecartin‘s father, Dell Trecartin, was a childhood friend ofKen Johnson (an art critic for the New York Times).
Johnson andLinda Norden(at that time, Norden was a curator atHarvard University’s Fogg Art Museum) attended the first public screening of an early film by Ryan Trecartin at the Rhode Island School of Design. The article goes on to state that Norden “would become one of Trecartin’s most effective supporters.”

## **The art world has its own version of the Hollywood dream**
### **Most artists only show you their success, no one talks about what’s difficult**
A lot of art schools bring successful, recent alums to lecture and speak about their experiences. Schools naturally want students to have a point of reference for what’s possible, so it makes sense to bring in the alums who have experienced that success early.
However, many of these successful recent alums giving these talks don’t bother to address the less glamorous parts of being an artist, any periods of struggle prior to their success, financial difficulties.
From the outside, the process of building a career in visual arts can appear to be a piece of cake. Social media only perpetuates this, as many young artists heavily curate their feeds to appear much happier and more successful than they actually are.

## **The art world has its own version of the Hollywood dream**
### **Every artist struggles at some point!**
All of this is hugely misleading to artists at the very beginning of their career, you feel like you are the only artist in the world who is having a hard time, that everyone else is more content, more active, younger, have had success much earlier than you!
In theory, it should be inspiring to hear these successful alums who attended the same art school. More often than not though, students feel very demoralized afterwards. Every year, I hear the same comments from students afterwards:
**_“I’m so depressed.”_**
**_“I’m never going to make it.”_**
**_“I’m so behind.”_**
**_“I’m already a junior and I haven’t done anything yet!”_**
> _**“Fear not: as grim as the career of an artist may look at times, there are more ways than ever to get your work out there and make it work! I found little success when I was just looking at book publishers.**_  
>   
>   
> _**Now that I’ve started meeting local bands, interacting with small businesses, and even joining a gallery (trust me, the last place I thought my work would fit!) I’m slowly finding people who I can work with as an artist.Be honest with your artwork, and the right venue for it will come.**_  
>   
>   
> _**Don’t try to make your work fit a specific goal, but try to find a goal that fits the kind of art you enjoy. In my experience, as I let go of the assumption that I knew what I wanted to do, I’ve been having so much more fun making my work again!**_**_”_**  
>   
> Alex Rowe  
>   
> Illustrator & Children’s Book Artist

## **The art world has its own version of the Hollywood dream**
### **Every artist struggles at some point!**
> _**“Sometimes I feel embarrassed that I lived with my parents for so long, but I try to be honest about it. Jobs in the art world can be competitive and many do not pay well especially when you’re just starting out.**_  
>   
>   
> _**Since I didn’t have the pressure of making rent for several years, I was able to put a lot of time and energy into my gallery position, studio, and professional relationships, while paying off my student loans.**_  
>   
>   
> _**Creating this network of social and professional support has been enormously helpful for my artistic and financial stability as I transition into my own place in New York City.”**_  
>   
> Lauryn Welch  
>   
> Painter & Performance Artist

## **The art world has its own version of the Hollywood dream**
### **Pursue what YOU want to do, not what everyone else says you should do**
Most of the time nowadays, I practically bolt out of bed and with feverish enthusiasm on my current projects. However, I still get self-conscious from time to time about taking an alternative path as an artist.
When that happens, I remember what my former professor said to me, and I can renew my confidence in the path I chose to take.
For many years after finished myMFA degree, I was trying to fulfillsomeone else’s checklist of goals that were not my own. Since I walked away from that checklist of goals, the world is a _much_ bigger place, and I’m seeing opportunities in places I never would have considered options even just 5 years ago.

## **The art world has its own version of the Hollywood dream**
### **Consider just having an active art practice a success**
What art schools should do (which they never will) is bring in recent alums who are just barely sustaining our artistic practice. Those of us who have had little or moderate success, but who are still actively producing their artwork.
For most of us, maintaining a studio practice is a long, tedious, incremental, slow slog that isn’t so easy.
However, in my opinion, maintaining an active studio practice is in itself an achievement to be recognized. It’s no small feat to juggle jobs, paying bills, family/friends, and everything else that life throws at you while simultaneously being able to find the head space and time to create on a long term basis.
Do what it takes to keep your art practice alive, _anything_ that motivates you is valid.

**Ian Joseph Somerhalder**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-Meroney-1) ( _SUM-ər-hawl-dər_; born December 8, 1978) is an American retired actor. He is known for playing Boone Carlyle in ABC's science fiction adventure drama television series _Lost_ (2004–2010) and Damon Salvatore in the CW supernatural teen drama series _The Vampire Diaries_ (2009–2017).

## Early life
Somerhalder was born on December 8, 1978,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-2) in Covington, Louisiana.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-Hello_Mag-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-5) His mother, Edna (née Israel),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-6) is a massage therapist of Choctaw and Irish descent[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-7) from Mississippi,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-Minnick-8) while his father, Robert Somerhalder Sr., is an independent building contractor[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-knutzen-9) of Cajun descent.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-Meroney-1)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-Chassen-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-Highfill-11) The second of three children, Somerhalder has an elder brother and a younger sister.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-Rickman-12):2[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-Cave-13)

## Early life
Somerhalder graduated from [Saint Paul's School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Paul's_School_(Louisiana) "St. Paul's School (Louisiana)").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-14) He embarked on a modeling career from age 10[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-knutzen-9)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-Cave-13) to 13.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-15) His parents divorced[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-Meroney-1) when he was 14, and he subsequently lived with his mother.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-Rickman-12):3 At age 17, Somerhalder decided to refocus on acting[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-Hello_Mag-4) and began studying with acting teacher William Esper.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-Rickman-12):8[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-16)

## Career
Somerhalder at the 2015 _Wizard World_ Convention
In the summer of 2000, Somerhalder starred in the short-lived WB series _Young Americans_, a spin-off of _[Dawson's Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dawson's\_Creek "Dawson's Creek")_. He played Hamilton Fleming, the son of the dean of a prestigious boarding school. In 2002, Somerhalder played bisexual character Paul Denton in Roger Avary's adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis' novel, _The Rules of Attraction_, alongside James Van Der Beek, Shannyn Sossamon, and Jessica Biel.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-17)
In 2004, Somerhalder scored his breakthrough role when he played Boone Carlyle in _Lost_. Despite his character's death in the twentieth episode of the first season, he returned to the role of Boone for seven more episodes between 2005 and 2010, including the series finale. He was the first major character to die.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-Malcom-18) Following his departure from the show, ABC signed him to another one-year contract.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-19) In 2005, he stated that being a part of _Lost_ was "the greatest experience" of "the greatest year of his life".[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-Williamson-21)

## Career
In 2009, Somerhalder appeared in the movie _The Tournament_ where he played the role of an assassin participating in a lethal competition with other assassins. He appears in the coffee table book _About Face_ by celebrity photographer John Russo.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-23) Also in 2009, Somerhalder began playing the role of Vampire Damon Salvatore as a series regular in The CW television drama series _The Vampire Diaries_. The series premiere attracted The CW's highest premiere ratings of any season premiere since the network began in 2006. The series has continued to be the highest-rated series on its channel with both his performance and the show receiving a positive response from critics. He began directing _The Vampire Diaries_ in its third season and produced the series at the start of season 8. He received several Teen Choice Awards and a [People's Choice Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Choice_Award "People's Choice Award") for his participation on the series.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-24)
Somerhalder acted in the short subject _Time Framed_ (2013).[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-25) He played Dr. Luther Swann as a series regular in the Netflixscience fictionhorror series _V Wars_, which ran from 2019 to 2020.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-28)

## Career
In 2020, Somerhalder shot footage for and served as an executive producer on the film _Kiss the Ground,_ a documentary centered on regenerative agriculture.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-29) He returned as an executive producer on its follow-up documentary, _Common Ground_, in 2023.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-30)
In a 2024 interview, Somerhalder revealed that he had retired from acting after relocating to a farm outside of Los Angeles, though he would still be involved in producing and environmental activism.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-31)

## Foundations and causes
Paul Wesley, Nina Dobrev and Somerhalder in 2012
Somerhalder was involved in the cleanup after the _Deepwater Horizon_ oil drilling disaster on April 22, 2010. His efforts included cleaning of oiled wildlife and taping public service announcements to let the public know how they could help.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-32) Somerhalder also supports the St. Tammany Humane Society, an organization for animal shelter and welfare. On November 13, 2010, he hosted a Bash on the Bayou charity fundraiser for the Society. During the event, Somerhalder was presented with a donation of $11,100 by _The Vampire Diaries_fandom for his birthday project.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-36)
Together with his _The Vampire Diaries_ co-stars Candice Accola and Michael Trevino, Somerhalder supports the It Gets Better Project, which makes it a goal to prevent suicide among LGBT youth[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-37) associated with The Trevor Project.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-38) For his second campaign, Somerhalder teamed up with _The Vampire Diaries_ co-star Paul Wesley to release a limited edition shirt designed by a fan, with the words "Blood Brothers Since 1864."[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-39) This campaign sold almost 10,000 shirts.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-40)

## Foundations and causes
On December 8, 2010, Somerhalder's 32nd birthday, he launched the "Ian Somerhalder Foundation" which he hopes will educate people on the importance of protecting the environment and animals: "Instead of gifts this year, my birthday wish is that we come together and raise funds to support projects that protect our habitat and nurture our furry friends."[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-42) To spread awareness for his foundation, Somerhalder sponsors and often walks in Mardi Paws, a parade and organization held in his hometown of Covington.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-43) He opposes GMO foods and factory farming, and supports ecologistAllan Savory in his crusade to let cows graze in sync with nature to enrich soil, enhance biodiversity, and reverse climate change. In 2011, Somerhalder visited Savory in Africa and announced he was making a documentary about him with the goal of winning him a Nobel Prize.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-isfsavory-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-esavory-45)
Somerhalder is also a celebrity campaigner for RYOT, a Los Angeles-based media company known for RYOT.org, its cause-based, take action online news source.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-46)

## Personal life
Somerhalder dated his _Vampire Diaries_ co-star Nina Dobrev from 2010 to 2013.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-47) In 2014, he began dating actress Nikki Reed.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-48) They married on April 26, 2015, in Malibu, California.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-49) They had a daughter in 2017,[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-51) and a son in 2023.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-52)
While working on _Lost,_ Somerhalder and Maggie Grace adopted a feral cat named Roo which that they found "literally dying" in the jungle, and it later became Grace's "travel buddy."[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-53) Somerhalder stated that being a part of _Lost_ was "the greatest experience" of "the greatest year of his life".[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-55)

## Personal life
### Brother's Bond Bourbon
Somerhalder has remained close friends with his former _Vampire Diaries_ co-star Paul Wesley, and in 2020, they announced the launch of a straight bourbon whiskey named Brother's Bond Bourbon.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Somerhalder#cite_note-57)

Title: Ian Somerhalder Reveals ‘Controversial’ Reason He Left Hollywood and ‘Pulled the Plug’ on His Acting Career
Chunks: 0,1
### NEED TO KNOW
*   Ian Somerhalder stepped away from Hollywood in August 2019

*   In a new interview, he revealed the "really honest" reason behind his exit, which was a result of _V Wars_' cancellation

*   "I am not here for my career and livelihood to be dictated by someone who has mommy or daddy issues, or they weren't popular in school," he said
Nearly seven years after his exit, Ian Somerhalder is finally revealing the true reason he quit acting.
Somerhalder, 47, departed Hollywood in August 2019 and has since turned his focus to other business ventures with his wife, Nikki Reed, after they moved to a Calif. farm.
He shared the "really honest, kind of controversial" reason that he decided to pivot on the July 9 episode of the _Haley on the Go_ podcast, as he recalled how the cancellation of his Netflix series, _V Wars_, affected him.
"I wanted to do _V Wars_ because it was me, not as a vampire, it was me as a scientist," he said of the series. "[We] shot the show, moved my whole family to Northern Ontario. Worked really hard on this thing for almost a year, and the show that got turned in wasn't even watchable."
"I said to the studio, I don't want to put my name on this. I'll give you the money back — I'll give you millions of dollars. And they were like, 'What? What are you talking about?' "
_Ian Somerhalder in 'V Wars'_
_Credit: Netflix_
Somerhalder claimed he told Netflix that he and his producing partner, James Gibb, needed "creative control of the show" to fix it. "Netflix said, 'Sure. We're not giving you a dollar more.' "
He and Gibb raised more than $6 million to fix the series, Somerhalder said, and filmed "10 or 12 hours of footage in about six days," which landed him "in the hospital" from overworking his body.

### NEED TO KNOW
When the show premiered in December 2019, it was a "hit," Somerhalder said, but it was canceled anyway. Somerhalder alleged, "The execs were fighting, and someone quietly canceled the show. And the powers that be at Netflix were like, 'It's unfortunate. Yes, it shouldn't have happened. We can't go back, because it would set a precedent that would be terrible, so the show is done.' "
"I looked at myself in the mirror, and I said to my wife, I was like, man, I'm 40 years old. I don't want to spend two years of my life doing something, working this hard — one year fully unpaid — for this executive who had issues in high school, so they want to exert power now, [to cancel it]," Somerhalder said. "I am not here for my career and livelihood to be dictated by someone who has mommy or daddy issues, or they weren't popular in school."
"So I pulled the plug. That was it. I walked away," he said. "These executives are bitching at each other, and I'm like, are you kidding me? Done. I'm out."
Never miss a story — sign up for PEOPLE's free daily newsletter to stay up-to-date on the best of what PEOPLE has to offer, from celebrity news to compelling human interest stories.
_Nikki Reed and Ian Somerhalder at the EMA Awards Gala at Radford Studio Center on October 26, 2024_
_Credit: Gregg DeGuire/Getty_
There's a possibility, albeit slim, of Somerhalder making a return to Hollywood. In 2024, he told PEOPLE that acting is "in the rearview mirror," but also shared a more positive update.
"We got the rights back for _V Wars_," he revealed. "But I just don't know how the hell we would ever make a TV show."
