**Christopher Larkin Stephens** (born 19 June 1967) is an English actor.
Born Christopher Stephens on 19 June 1967 at Middlesex Hospital in London,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Larkin#cite_note-1) Larkin is the elder son of actors Dame Maggie Smith and Sir Robert Stephens. His younger brother is actor Toby Stephens. Larkin revealed in an interview that he chose his stage name in order to distance himself from his famous parents, not wanting "to trade on the family connection", and selected "_Larkin"_ in honor of his favorite poet, Philip Larkin.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Larkin#cite_note-Daily_Express_Name_Change-2)
Larkin trained at the London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art (LAMDA). He is best known for playing Hermann Göring in the film _Hitler: The Rise of Evil_, but also played Charles Darwin for the PBS series _Evolution_ and the abolitionist William Wilberforce in the radio production of _Grace Victorious_. Larkin also played Captain Howard of the Marines in Peter Weir's _Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World_ alongside Paul Bettany and Russell Crowe, and appeared in _Valkyrie_ with Tom Cruise playing Sgt. Helm. Other film credits are _Angels and Insects_, Franco Zeffirelli's _Jane Eyre_ and _Tea with Mussolini_, and _Heroes and Villains_ directed by Selwyn Roberts.

Larkin played Cambridge, a minicab driver who went to university_[who?_] in series 1 and 2 of John Sullivan's _Roger Roger_ for BBC1 and portrayed George Marston_[who?_] in Charles Sturridge's _Shackleton_ for Channel Four. Larkin also appeared in the 2007 episode of _Doctor Who_ "The Shakespeare Code" and the 2012 low-budget horror film _The Facility_ (originally titled _Guinea Pigs_) directed by Ian Clark.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Larkin#cite_note-3) He appeared in three episodes of the fourth season of _Black Sails_, starring his brother, Toby Stephens.
In 2013 he starred in the television revival of _Yes, Prime Minister_ as Bernard Woolley,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Larkin#cite_note-4) reprising the role he had played in the Gielgud Theatre in London's West End.
Other theatre credits include: Edgar in _The Lady from Dubuque_ starring his mother, Maggie Smith, and directed by Anthony Page; Jopari in Nicholas Hytner's production of _His Dark Materials_ at The National Theatre; _The Whisky Taster_ by James Graham at the Bush Theatre, London; and the nationwide tour of _Noises Off_, directed by Lindsay Posner.

# Christopher Larkin
Christopher Larkin was an American actor and musician born in Daegu, South Korea. Adopted by American parents at four months old, Larkin was raised in Hebron, Connecticut. In 2001, he was cast in a Hallmark TV movie called "The Flamingo Rising," his acting debut. Larkin attended Greater Hartford Academy of the Arts and graduated in 2005, the same year he made his (uncredited) film debut in "Strangers With Candy" alongside Amy Sedaris and Stephen Colbert. Larkin then attended Fordham University in New York City, where he majored in theater. While there, he acted in several off-Broadway productions, and took time off during his senior year in 2008 to play the title character in the Steppenwolf Theatre Company's production of "Kafka on the Shore" in Chicago, Illinois. Larkin also acted in an episode of the long-running soap opera "One Life to Live" (ABC, 1968-2013) and lent his voice to the racing video game "Midnight Club: Los Angeles" in 2008, before graduating in 2009. In 2013, he appeared in an episode each of "90210" (The CW, 2008-2013) and "Awkward" (MTV, 2011-16). The next year, he landed his big break with a starring role on "The 100" (The CW, 2014-) a post-apocalyptic drama that grew more critically praised with each subsequent season. Larkin played Monty Green, an original member of the titular group.

# Chris Larkin
**Chris Larkin** is a British actor with a wide range of credits on both stage and screen.
Chris is the son of the late British actors Dame Maggie Smith and Sir Robert Stephens, and the brother of actor Toby Stephens.
Chris Larkin recently starred in _\_**The Gathered Leaves**\__ at Marylebone Theatre in London.
Chris Larkin’s theatre credits include:_Pack of Lies_(Menier Chocolate Factory);_Again_ (Trafalgar Studios);_Stevie_(Chichester Festival Theatre);_Noises Off_(The Old Vic);_Yes, Prime Minister_(National Tour and West End);_The Whisky Taster_(Bush Theatre);_The Lady from Dubuque_(Theatre Royal Haymarket);_His Dark Materials_(National Theatre);_A Midsummer Night’s Dream_(Regent’s Park Open Air Theatre);_Much Ado About Nothing_(Regent’s Park Open Air Theatre);_When We Are Married_(Festival Theatre and Savoy Theatre) and _Tess of the D’Urbervilles_(Derby and Salisbury Playhouse).
Chris’s screen credits include:_Professor T_(ITV);_Outlander_(Left Bank Pictures);_Next of Kin_,_Father Brown_,_WPC56_,_Doctors, Yes, Prime Minister_, After Thomas,_Doctor Who_,_Friends and Crocodiles_(BBC);_Black Sails_(Platinum Dunes);_Churchill’s Secret_(PBS);_Coalition_(Channel 4);_Marple_(ITV);_Mysterious Island_(Hallmark Entertainment);_Hitler: Rise of Evil (_ Alliance Atlantis Communications);_Rosemary and Thyme_(Carnival Film and Television);_Darwin_(WGBH);_Shackleton_(Channel 4); Casualty (BBC);_Highlander_(Rysher Entertainment);_Frank Stubbs Promotes_(Noel Gay Television);_Roger Roger_ and Karaoke(BBC).

**Christopher Larkin Stephens** (born 19 June 1967) is an English actor.
Born Christopher Stephens on 19 June 1967 at Middlesex Hospital in London,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Larkin#cite_note-1) Larkin is the elder son of actors Dame Maggie Smith and Sir Robert Stephens. His younger brother is actor Toby Stephens. Larkin revealed in an interview that he chose his stage name in order to distance himself from his famous parents, not wanting "to trade on the family connection", and selected "_Larkin"_ in honor of his favorite poet, Philip Larkin.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Larkin#cite_note-Daily_Express_Name_Change-2)
Larkin trained at the London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art (LAMDA). He is best known for playing Hermann Göring in the film _Hitler: The Rise of Evil_, but also played Charles Darwin for the PBS series _Evolution_ and the abolitionist William Wilberforce in the radio production of _Grace Victorious_. Larkin also played Captain Howard of the Marines in Peter Weir's _Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World_ alongside Paul Bettany and Russell Crowe, and appeared in _Valkyrie_ with Tom Cruise playing Sgt. Helm. Other film credits are _Angels and Insects_, Franco Zeffirelli's _Jane Eyre_ and _Tea with Mussolini_, and _Heroes and Villains_ directed by Selwyn Roberts.

Larkin played Cambridge, a minicab driver who went to university_[who?_] in series 1 and 2 of John Sullivan's _Roger Roger_ for BBC1 and portrayed George Marston_[who?_] in Charles Sturridge's _Shackleton_ for Channel Four. Larkin also appeared in the 2007 episode of _Doctor Who_ "The Shakespeare Code" and the 2012 low-budget horror film _The Facility_ (originally titled _Guinea Pigs_) directed by Ian Clark.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Larkin#cite_note-3) He appeared in three episodes of the fourth season of _Black Sails_, starring his brother, Toby Stephens.
In 2013 he starred in the television revival of _Yes, Prime Minister_ as Bernard Woolley,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Larkin#cite_note-4) reprising the role he had played in the Gielgud Theatre in London's West End.
Other theatre credits include: Edgar in _The Lady from Dubuque_ starring his mother, Maggie Smith, and directed by Anthony Page; Jopari in Nicholas Hytner's production of _His Dark Materials_ at The National Theatre; _The Whisky Taster_ by James Graham at the Bush Theatre, London; and the nationwide tour of _Noises Off_, directed by Lindsay Posner.

# Christopher Larkin
Christopher Larkin was an American actor and musician born in Daegu, South Korea. Adopted by American parents at four months old, Larkin was raised in Hebron, Connecticut. In 2001, he was cast in a Hallmark TV movie called "The Flamingo Rising," his acting debut. Larkin attended Greater Hartford Academy of the Arts and graduated in 2005, the same year he made his (uncredited) film debut in "Strangers With Candy" alongside Amy Sedaris and Stephen Colbert. Larkin then attended Fordham University in New York City, where he majored in theater. While there, he acted in several off-Broadway productions, and took time off during his senior year in 2008 to play the title character in the Steppenwolf Theatre Company's production of "Kafka on the Shore" in Chicago, Illinois. Larkin also acted in an episode of the long-running soap opera "One Life to Live" (ABC, 1968-2013) and lent his voice to the racing video game "Midnight Club: Los Angeles" in 2008, before graduating in 2009. In 2013, he appeared in an episode each of "90210" (The CW, 2008-2013) and "Awkward" (MTV, 2011-16). The next year, he landed his big break with a starring role on "The 100" (The CW, 2014-) a post-apocalyptic drama that grew more critically praised with each subsequent season. Larkin played Monty Green, an original member of the titular group.

**Christopher Larkin Stephens** (born 19 June 1967) is an English actor.
Born Christopher Stephens on 19 June 1967 at Middlesex Hospital in London,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Larkin#cite_note-1) Larkin is the elder son of actors Dame Maggie Smith and Sir Robert Stephens. His younger brother is actor Toby Stephens. Larkin revealed in an interview that he chose his stage name in order to distance himself from his famous parents, not wanting "to trade on the family connection", and selected "_Larkin"_ in honor of his favorite poet, Philip Larkin.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Larkin#cite_note-Daily_Express_Name_Change-2)
Larkin trained at the London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art (LAMDA). He is best known for playing Hermann Göring in the film _Hitler: The Rise of Evil_, but also played Charles Darwin for the PBS series _Evolution_ and the abolitionist William Wilberforce in the radio production of _Grace Victorious_. Larkin also played Captain Howard of the Marines in Peter Weir's _Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World_ alongside Paul Bettany and Russell Crowe, and appeared in _Valkyrie_ with Tom Cruise playing Sgt. Helm. Other film credits are _Angels and Insects_, Franco Zeffirelli's _Jane Eyre_ and _Tea with Mussolini_, and _Heroes and Villains_ directed by Selwyn Roberts.

Larkin played Cambridge, a minicab driver who went to university_[who?_] in series 1 and 2 of John Sullivan's _Roger Roger_ for BBC1 and portrayed George Marston_[who?_] in Charles Sturridge's _Shackleton_ for Channel Four. Larkin also appeared in the 2007 episode of _Doctor Who_ "The Shakespeare Code" and the 2012 low-budget horror film _The Facility_ (originally titled _Guinea Pigs_) directed by Ian Clark.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Larkin#cite_note-3) He appeared in three episodes of the fourth season of _Black Sails_, starring his brother, Toby Stephens.
In 2013 he starred in the television revival of _Yes, Prime Minister_ as Bernard Woolley,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Larkin#cite_note-4) reprising the role he had played in the Gielgud Theatre in London's West End.
Other theatre credits include: Edgar in _The Lady from Dubuque_ starring his mother, Maggie Smith, and directed by Anthony Page; Jopari in Nicholas Hytner's production of _His Dark Materials_ at The National Theatre; _The Whisky Taster_ by James Graham at the Bush Theatre, London; and the nationwide tour of _Noises Off_, directed by Lindsay Posner.

**Joseph Michael Manganiello** ( _MANG-gə-NEL-oh_; born December 28, 1976) is an American actor, author, and producer. His professional film career began when he played Flash Thompson in Sam Raimi's _Spider-Man_. His breakout role was as werewolf Alcide Herveaux in five seasons of the HBO series _True Blood_.

He is also known for his roles in films such as _Magic Mike,_ _Magic Mike XXL,_ _[Pee-wee's Big Holiday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pee-wee's\_Big\_Holiday "Pee-wee's Big Holiday"),_ _[What to Expect When You're Expecting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What\_to\_Expect\_When\_You're\_Expecting\_(film) "What to Expect When You're Expecting (film)")_, _Sabotage_, and _Rampage_. In late 2013, he became a published author when his first book, _Evolution_, was released by Simon & Schuster's Gallery Books.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-1) He also pubished his second book in 2026, Bloodlines, released by Simon & Schuster's and became a National Bestseler in its first week.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-2) His directorial debut came in 2014 with the documentary feature _La Bare_, which he also produced and financed. He is also known for his role as Brad Morris in _How I Met Your Mother_. He is active with several charities, primarily [UPMC Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UPMC_Children's_Hospital_of_Pittsburgh "UPMC Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh") for which he serves on the board of trustees. In 2016, he was cast as Slade Wilson / Deathstroke in the DC Extended Universe, making his first appearance in 2017's _Justice League_.

Manganiello was born in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, to Susan and Charles Manganiello.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-3) He has a younger brother, Nicholas. His mother is of Armenian, Croatian, and German descent.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-vulture-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-AGBU-6) Manganiello's father was born in Massachusetts outside of Boston.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-fdr2-7) Joe Manganiello was raised in Mt. Lebanon, Pennsylvania, an affluent suburb of Pittsburgh bordering the city.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-8) Raised Catholic, he was a student at St. Bernard School, a Catholic elementary school in Mt. Lebanon, Pennsylvania and then attended Mt. Lebanon High School, where he graduated with honors in 1995 and won the school's Great Alumni Award in 2011.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Randall-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Niederberger-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Owen-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-13)

Growing up, he was the captain of his football, basketball, and volleyball teams and went on to play at the varsity level in all three sports.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Randall-9) He won the role of Jud Fry in his school's senior year production of _Oklahoma!_ and was involved with the school's TV studio. He would borrow equipment in order to write and direct films with his friends, which eventually inspired him to begin studying acting.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Owen-12)
Manganiello suffered a series of sports injuries through high school, including a torn medial collateral ligament while returning a kickoff in a varsity football game against Ringgold High School. The time off allowed Manganiello to reevaluate his future and so he decided to audition for the Carnegie Mellon School of Drama during his senior year. He was not accepted, so he enrolled at the University of Pittsburgh and worked over the next year in the theater. He then reapplied to Carnegie Mellon a year later, and was awarded a scholarship, accepted into the acting program that year.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Randall-9) There he performed in theater productions and wrote, produced, and acted in a student film entitled _Out of Courage 2: Out for Vengeance_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Weiskind-14) He graduated in 2000 with a Bachelor of Fine Arts degree in acting.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Owen-12) He then traveled to New York City and Los Angeles through his university to participate in group auditions, which provided him contacts in the entertainment business including an agent, a manager, and a screen test for Sam Raimi's _Spider-Man_.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Williamson-15)

In the February 7, 2023, episode of PBS series _Finding Your Roots_, the researchers uncovered that Manganiello's legal paternal grandfather, Emilio Manganiello,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-today-16) was not his biological grandfather, and that his biological great-grandparents were an African-American man named William Henry Cutler and a white woman named Nellie Alton. His biological paternal grandfather was one of Cutler and Alton's three mixed-race African-American sons.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-rolling-17)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-fdr2-7) Using this information, researchers traced Manganiello's paternal lineage back to his great-great-great-great-great-grandfather, Plato Turner, an African slave who was freed before slavery was abolished in Massachusetts and who went on to fight for the Continental Army during the American Revolution.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-fdr2-7)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-today-16) Manganiello's maternal great-grandmother, Terviz "Rose" Darakjian,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-rolling-17) was a survivor of the Armenian genocide, where her husband and seven of her children were killed. Darakjian's eighth child, an infant, drowned during Darakjian's escape across the Euphrates River.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-fdr2-7) Darakjian later encountered Karl Wilhelm Beutinger, a German soldier, in an internment camp for survivors. Rose became pregnant by him. Beutinger soon left to return to Germany. He resumed his life there with his German wife and children, and never saw Rose Darakjian again.

Title: uk news on Instagram: "Chadwick Boseman: A Legacy That Continues to Inspire

Chadwick Boseman was one of the most respected actors of his generation, remembered for his powerful performances, quiet determination and extraordinary impact on audiences around the world.

Born on November 29, 1976, in Anderson, South Carolina, Boseman studied directing at Howard University before pursuing a career in acting. He initially worked in television and theater, gradually building a reputation for portraying important historical figures with depth and dignity.

Breakthrough With 42

Boseman’s major breakthrough came with the 2013 film 42, in which he portrayed baseball legend Jackie Robinson. His performance brought Robinson’s courage and determination to a new generation of viewers.

The following year, he played music icon James Brown in Get on Up, demonstrating his ability to transform himself physically and emotionally for demanding roles.

Becoming Black Panther

In 2016, Boseman made his first appearance as T’Challa, the Black Panther, in Captain America: Civil War. He subsequently reprised the character in Black Panther, Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame.

Black Panther became a cultural phenomenon, and Boseman’s portrayal of T’Challa turned him into an international star. The character represented leadership, strength and cultural pride for millions of fans.

A Versatile Performer

Boseman continued taking on challenging roles outside the superhero genre. He portrayed Thurgood Marshall in Marshall and appeared in films including 21 Bridges, Da 5 Bloods and Ma Rainey’s Black Bottom.

His final film performances demonstrated the remarkable range of an actor whose career was tragically cut short.

A Lasting Legacy

Chadwick Boseman died on August 28, 2020, at the age of 43, following a private battle with colon cancer.

His death shocked the entertainment world, but his work continues to resonate. Beyond his performances, Boseman became admired for his professionalism, humility and commitment to meaningful storytelling.

His portrayal of T’Challa, Jackie Robinson, James Brown, Thurgood Marshall and other memorable characters remains an important part of modern cinema"

**Joseph Michael Manganiello** ( _MANG-gə-NEL-oh_; born December 28, 1976) is an American actor, author, and producer. His professional film career began when he played Flash Thompson in Sam Raimi's _Spider-Man_. His breakout role was as werewolf Alcide Herveaux in five seasons of the HBO series _True Blood_.
texts.1: He is also known for his roles in films such as _Magic Mike,_ _Magic Mike XXL,_ _[Pee-wee's Big Holiday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pee-wee's\_Big\_Holiday "Pee-wee's Big Holiday"),_ _[What to Expect When You're Expecting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What\_to\_Expect\_When\_You're\_Expecting\_(film) "What to Expect When You're Expecting (film)")_, _Sabotage_, and _Rampage_. In late 2013, he became a published author when his first book, _Evolution_, was released by Simon & Schuster's Gallery Books.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-1) He also pubished his second book in 2026, Bloodlines, released by Simon & Schuster's and became a National Bestseler in its first week.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-2) His directorial debut came in 2014 with the documentary feature _La Bare_, which he also produced and financed. He is also known for his role as Brad Morris in _How I Met Your Mother_. He is active with several charities, primarily [UPMC Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UPMC_Children's_Hospital_of_Pittsburgh "UPMC Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh") for which he serves on the board of trustees. In 2016, he was cast as Slade Wilson / Deathstroke in the DC Extended Universe, making his first appearance in 2017's _Justice League_.
texts.2: Manganiello was born in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, to Susan and Charles Manganiello.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-3) He has a younger brother, Nicholas. His mother is of Armenian, Croatian, and German descent.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-vulture-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-AGBU-6) Manganiello's father was born in Massachusetts outside of Boston.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-fdr2-7) Joe Manganiello was raised in Mt. Lebanon, Pennsylvania, an affluent suburb of Pittsburgh bordering the city.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-8) Raised Catholic, he was a student at St. Bernard School, a Catholic elementary school in Mt. Lebanon, Pennsylvania and then attended Mt. Lebanon High School, where he graduated with honors in 1995 and won the school's Great Alumni Award in 2011.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Randall-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Niederberger-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Owen-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-13)
texts.3:
Growing up, he was the captain of his football, basketball, and volleyball teams and went on to play at the varsity level in all three sports.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Randall-9) He won the role of Jud Fry in his school's senior year production of _Oklahoma!_ and was involved with the school's TV studio. He would borrow equipment in order to write and direct films with his friends, which eventually inspired him to begin studying acting.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Owen-12)
Manganiello suffered a series of sports injuries through high school, including a torn medial collateral ligament while returning a kickoff in a varsity football game against Ringgold High School. The time off allowed Manganiello to reevaluate his future and so he decided to audition for the Carnegie Mellon School of Drama during his senior year. He was not accepted, so he enrolled at the University of Pittsburgh and worked over the next year in the theater. He then reapplied to Carnegie Mellon a year later, and was awarded a scholarship, accepted into the acting program that year.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Randall-9) There he performed in theater productions and wrote, produced, and acted in a student film entitled _Out of Courage 2: Out for Vengeance_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Weiskind-14) He graduated in 2000 with a Bachelor of Fine Arts degree in acting.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Owen-12) He then traveled to New York City and Los Angeles through his university to participate in group auditions, which provided him contacts in the entertainment business including an agent, a manager, and a screen test for Sam Raimi's _Spider-Man_.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Williamson-15)
texts.4: In the February 7, 2023, episode of PBS series _Finding Your Roots_, the researchers uncovered that Manganiello's legal paternal grandfather, Emilio Manganiello,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-today-16) was not his biological grandfather, and that his biological great-grandparents were an African-American man named William Henry Cutler and a white woman named Nellie Alton. His biological paternal grandfather was one of Cutler and Alton's three mixed-race African-American sons.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-rolling-17)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-fdr2-7) Using this information, researchers traced Manganiello's paternal lineage back to his great-great-great-great-great-grandfather, Plato Turner, an African slave who was freed before slavery was abolished in Massachusetts and who went on to fight for the Continental Army during the American Revolution.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-fdr2-7)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-today-16) Manganiello's maternal great-grandmother, Terviz "Rose" Darakjian,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-rolling-17) was a survivor of the Armenian genocide, where her husband and seven of her children were killed. Darakjian's eighth child, an infant, drowned during Darakjian's escape across the Euphrates River.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-fdr2-7) Darakjian later encountered Karl Wilhelm Beutinger, a German soldier, in an internment camp for survivors. Rose became pregnant by him. Beutinger soon left to return to Germany. He resumed his life there with his German wife and children, and never saw Rose Darakjian again.

Becoming Black Panther

Black Panther became a cultural phenomenon, and Boseman’s portrayal of T’Challa turned him into an international star. The character represented leadership, strength and cultural pride for millions of fans.

Boseman continued taking on challenging roles outside the superhero genre. He portrayed Thurgood Marshall in Marshall and appeared in films including 21 Bridges, Da 5 Bloods and Ma Rainey’s Black Bottom.

**Joseph Michael Manganiello** ( _MANG-gə-NEL-oh_; born December 28, 1976) is an American actor, author, and producer. His professional film career began when he played Flash Thompson in Sam Raimi's _Spider-Man_. His breakout role was as werewolf Alcide Herveaux in five seasons of the HBO series _True Blood_.

He is also known for his roles in films such as _Magic Mike,_ _Magic Mike XXL,_ _[Pee-wee's Big Holiday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pee-wee's\_Big\_Holiday "Pee-wee's Big Holiday"),_ _[What to Expect When You're Expecting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What\_to\_Expect\_When\_You're\_Expecting\_(film) "What to Expect When You're Expecting (film)")_, _Sabotage_, and _Rampage_. In late 2013, he became a published author when his first book, _Evolution_, was released by Simon & Schuster's Gallery Books.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-1) He also pubished his second book in 2026, Bloodlines, released by Simon & Schuster's and became a National Bestseler in its first week.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-2) His directorial debut came in 2014 with the documentary feature _La Bare_, which he also produced and financed. He is also known for his role as Brad Morris in _How I Met Your Mother_. He is active with several charities, primarily [UPMC Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UPMC_Children's_Hospital_of_Pittsburgh "UPMC Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh") for which he serves on the board of trustees. In 2016, he was cast as Slade Wilson / Deathstroke in the DC Extended Universe, making his first appearance in 2017's _Justice League_.

Manganiello was born in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, to Susan and Charles Manganiello.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-3) He has a younger brother, Nicholas. His mother is of Armenian, Croatian, and German descent.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-vulture-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-AGBU-6) Manganiello's father was born in Massachusetts outside of Boston.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-fdr2-7) Joe Manganiello was raised in Mt. Lebanon, Pennsylvania, an affluent suburb of Pittsburgh bordering the city.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-8) Raised Catholic, he was a student at St. Bernard School, a Catholic elementary school in Mt. Lebanon, Pennsylvania and then attended Mt. Lebanon High School, where he graduated with honors in 1995 and won the school's Great Alumni Award in 2011.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Randall-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Niederberger-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Owen-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-13)

Growing up, he was the captain of his football, basketball, and volleyball teams and went on to play at the varsity level in all three sports.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Randall-9) He won the role of Jud Fry in his school's senior year production of _Oklahoma!_ and was involved with the school's TV studio. He would borrow equipment in order to write and direct films with his friends, which eventually inspired him to begin studying acting.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Owen-12)
Manganiello suffered a series of sports injuries through high school, including a torn medial collateral ligament while returning a kickoff in a varsity football game against Ringgold High School. The time off allowed Manganiello to reevaluate his future and so he decided to audition for the Carnegie Mellon School of Drama during his senior year. He was not accepted, so he enrolled at the University of Pittsburgh and worked over the next year in the theater. He then reapplied to Carnegie Mellon a year later, and was awarded a scholarship, accepted into the acting program that year.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Randall-9) There he performed in theater productions and wrote, produced, and acted in a student film entitled _Out of Courage 2: Out for Vengeance_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Weiskind-14) He graduated in 2000 with a Bachelor of Fine Arts degree in acting.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Owen-12) He then traveled to New York City and Los Angeles through his university to participate in group auditions, which provided him contacts in the entertainment business including an agent, a manager, and a screen test for Sam Raimi's _Spider-Man_.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-Williamson-15)

In the February 7, 2023, episode of PBS series _Finding Your Roots_, the researchers uncovered that Manganiello's legal paternal grandfather, Emilio Manganiello,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-today-16) was not his biological grandfather, and that his biological great-grandparents were an African-American man named William Henry Cutler and a white woman named Nellie Alton. His biological paternal grandfather was one of Cutler and Alton's three mixed-race African-American sons.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-rolling-17)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-fdr2-7) Using this information, researchers traced Manganiello's paternal lineage back to his great-great-great-great-great-grandfather, Plato Turner, an African slave who was freed before slavery was abolished in Massachusetts and who went on to fight for the Continental Army during the American Revolution.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-fdr2-7)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-today-16) Manganiello's maternal great-grandmother, Terviz "Rose" Darakjian,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-rolling-17) was a survivor of the Armenian genocide, where her husband and seven of her children were killed. Darakjian's eighth child, an infant, drowned during Darakjian's escape across the Euphrates River.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Manganiello#cite_note-fdr2-7) Darakjian later encountered Karl Wilhelm Beutinger, a German soldier, in an internment camp for survivors. Rose became pregnant by him. Beutinger soon left to return to Germany. He resumed his life there with his German wife and children, and never saw Rose Darakjian again.

# Everything to Know About the Fertility Fraud Documentary ‘Our Father’
Inside the sinister true story of Donald Cline.  * * *
By Lydia Wang April 15, 2022  Link copied to clipboard Share
Jacoba Ballard always knew she was conceived via sperm donation. But when she decided to take a DNA test to learn more about her biological background, she didn’t expect to find a seemingly endless roster of half-siblings. After months of research and conversations with her many 23andMe matches, Ballard began to piece together the disturbing truth: Donald Cline, a man known as one of the most renowned fertility experts in Indiana, had inseminated dozens of women with his own sperm without their consent or knowledge.
“The majority of us live in a 25-mile radius of each other,” Ballard says in the trailer for the documentary. “I walk around, and I can be related to everyone. I dread every new match that comes, but they just keep coming.”
Ahead, everything to know about Ballard, Cline and the real story behind _Our Father_ before it premieres this May.

# Everything to Know About the Fertility Fraud Documentary ‘Our Father’
### What is _Our Father_ about?
_Our Father_ tells the story of Jacoba Ballard and her half-siblings — over 50 people in total — who discovered that they were all paternally related through Donald Cline, a former fertility doctor in Indianapolis. The doc follows the criminal investigation into Cline’s actions, his possible motives and the compounding impact of his lies and abuse. It also examines the legalities around fertility fraud and how the newfound accessibility in genealogy testing, through companies like 23andMe, has uncovered more stories like Cline’s.

# Everything to Know About the Fertility Fraud Documentary ‘Our Father’
### Who is Donald Cline?
Don Cline was known as a premier fertility expert. As one person says in _Our Father_’s trailer, “Dr. Cline was the best infertility doctor in Indianapolis.” But this image of Cline was destroyed after an investigation found he had used his own sperm to inseminate his patients — without their knowledge or consent — dozens of times, resulting in his paternity of at least 50 children, all born in the ’70s and ’80s. Since this type of fertility fraud isn’t considered a crime under federal or Indiana state law, Cline’s victims struggled to find adequate legal justice. Cline retired from practice in 2009, and in 2017 he was convicted on two felony counts for obstructing the investigation. In 2018, the Medical Licensing Board of Indiana moved to prohibit him from applying to reinstate his license in the future.

# Everything to Know About the Fertility Fraud Documentary ‘Our Father’
### How did Don Cline’s children find out he was their father?
According to a 2019 deep dive in _The Atlantic_, Ballard was one of the first to piece together the details. She told the publication that she found her first half-sister on an online forum for donor-conceived children, and they connected over the fact that their parents both worked with Cline. When she looked the woman up on Facebook, she was struck by their physical similarities. That’s when Ballard and her half-sister decided to get at-home DNA kits, and not only discovered that they were related but that there were even _more_ siblings out there.
They weren’t alone in their discovery. In _Our Father_’s trailer, some of Cline’s other children say that they also learned about him through DNA kits. “When I opened up Ancestry, I had over 3,000 hits,” one recalls. “All of these random names were popping up, and it said ‘Close Family,’ ” says another.

# Everything to Know About the Fertility Fraud Documentary ‘Our Father’
### What is genetic genealogy?

# Everything to Know About the Fertility Fraud Documentary ‘Our Father’
Inside the sinister true story of Donald Cline.  * * *
By Lydia Wang April 15, 2022  Link copied to clipboard Share
Jacoba Ballard always knew she was conceived via sperm donation. But when she decided to take a DNA test to learn more about her biological background, she didn’t expect to find a seemingly endless roster of half-siblings. After months of research and conversations with her many 23andMe matches, Ballard began to piece together the disturbing truth: Donald Cline, a man known as one of the most renowned fertility experts in Indiana, had inseminated dozens of women with his own sperm without their consent or knowledge.
“The majority of us live in a 25-mile radius of each other,” Ballard says in the trailer for the documentary. “I walk around, and I can be related to everyone. I dread every new match that comes, but they just keep coming.”
Ahead, everything to know about Ballard, Cline and the real story behind _Our Father_ before it premieres this May.
texts.2:
# Everything to Know About the Fertility Fraud Documentary ‘Our Father’
### What is _Our Father_ about?
_Our Father_ tells the story of Jacoba Ballard and her half-siblings — over 50 people in total — who discovered that they were all paternally related through Donald Cline, a former fertility doctor in Indianapolis. The doc follows the criminal investigation into Cline’s actions, his possible motives and the compounding impact of his lies and abuse. It also examines the legalities around fertility fraud and how the newfound accessibility in genealogy testing, through companies like 23andMe, has uncovered more stories like Cline’s.
texts.3:
# Everything to Know About the Fertility Fraud Documentary ‘Our Father’
### Who is Donald Cline?
Don Cline was known as a premier fertility expert. As one person says in _Our Father_’s trailer, “Dr. Cline was the best infertility doctor in Indianapolis.” But this image of Cline was destroyed after an investigation found he had used his own sperm to inseminate his patients — without their knowledge or consent — dozens of times, resulting in his paternity of at least 50 children, all born in the ’70s and ’80s. Since this type of fertility fraud isn’t considered a crime under federal or Indiana state law, Cline’s victims struggled to find adequate legal justice. Cline retired from practice in 2009, and in 2017 he was convicted on two felony counts for obstructing the investigation. In 2018, the Medical Licensing Board of Indiana moved to prohibit him from applying to reinstate his license in the future.

# Everything to Know About the Fertility Fraud Documentary ‘Our Father’
### How did Don Cline’s children find out he was their father?
According to a 2019 deep dive in _The Atlantic_, Ballard was one of the first to piece together the details. She told the publication that she found her first half-sister on an online forum for donor-conceived children, and they connected over the fact that their parents both worked with Cline. When she looked the woman up on Facebook, she was struck by their physical similarities. That’s when Ballard and her half-sister decided to get at-home DNA kits, and not only discovered that they were related but that there were even _more_ siblings out there.
They weren’t alone in their discovery. In _Our Father_’s trailer, some of Cline’s other children say that they also learned about him through DNA kits. “When I opened up Ancestry, I had over 3,000 hits,” one recalls. “All of these random names were popping up, and it said ‘Close Family,’ ” says another.

It’s only been since starting the podcast and talking to more adopted and donor conceived people, recipient parents and donors that I have changed my stance on it. Seeing it from the children’s perspective on how it impacts them, which, in a lot of cases, is more than meeting their donor. A lot of recipient parents say they want it to be their child’s decision, but a child doesn’t understand the implications of that decision until they’re much older. # Everything to Know About the Fertility Fraud Documentary ‘Our Father’
Inside the sinister true story of Donald Cline.  * * *
By Lydia Wang April 15, 2022  Link copied to clipboard Share
Jacoba Ballard always knew she was conceived via sperm donation. But when she decided to take a DNA test to learn more about her biological background, she didn’t expect to find a seemingly endless roster of half-siblings. After months of research and conversations with her many 23andMe matches, Ballard began to piece together the disturbing truth: Donald Cline, a man known as one of the most renowned fertility experts in Indiana, had inseminated dozens of women with his own sperm without their consent or knowledge.
“The majority of us live in a 25-mile radius of each other,” Ballard says in the trailer for the documentary. “I walk around, and I can be related to everyone. I dread every new match that comes, but they just keep coming.”
Ahead, everything to know about Ballard, Cline and the real story behind _Our Father_ before it premieres this May.

# Everything to Know About the Fertility Fraud Documentary ‘Our Father’
### What is _Our Father_ about?
_Our Father_ tells the story of Jacoba Ballard and her half-siblings — over 50 people in total — who discovered that they were all paternally related through Donald Cline, a former fertility doctor in Indianapolis. The doc follows the criminal investigation into Cline’s actions, his possible motives and the compounding impact of his lies and abuse. It also examines the legalities around fertility fraud and how the newfound accessibility in genealogy testing, through companies like 23andMe, has uncovered more stories like Cline’s.

# Everything to Know About the Fertility Fraud Documentary ‘Our Father’
### Who is Donald Cline?
Don Cline was known as a premier fertility expert. As one person says in _Our Father_’s trailer, “Dr. Cline was the best infertility doctor in Indianapolis.” But this image of Cline was destroyed after an investigation found he had used his own sperm to inseminate his patients — without their knowledge or consent — dozens of times, resulting in his paternity of at least 50 children, all born in the ’70s and ’80s. Since this type of fertility fraud isn’t considered a crime under federal or Indiana state law, Cline’s victims struggled to find adequate legal justice. Cline retired from practice in 2009, and in 2017 he was convicted on two felony counts for obstructing the investigation. In 2018, the Medical Licensing Board of Indiana moved to prohibit him from applying to reinstate his license in the future.

# Everything to Know About the Fertility Fraud Documentary ‘Our Father’
### How did Don Cline’s children find out he was their father?
According to a 2019 deep dive in _The Atlantic_, Ballard was one of the first to piece together the details. She told the publication that she found her first half-sister on an online forum for donor-conceived children, and they connected over the fact that their parents both worked with Cline. When she looked the woman up on Facebook, she was struck by their physical similarities. That’s when Ballard and her half-sister decided to get at-home DNA kits, and not only discovered that they were related but that there were even _more_ siblings out there.
They weren’t alone in their discovery. In _Our Father_’s trailer, some of Cline’s other children say that they also learned about him through DNA kits. “When I opened up Ancestry, I had over 3,000 hits,” one recalls. “All of these random names were popping up, and it said ‘Close Family,’ ” says another.

# Everything to Know About the Fertility Fraud Documentary ‘Our Father’
### What is genetic genealogy?
Genetic genealogy is the use of DNA tests (including at-home kits like 23andMe) to reveal a person’s biological relatives and background. It’s often used to solve forensic cases, but it’s also an increasingly common way for adopted and donor-conceived children, like Ballard and her half-siblings, to learn more about their ancestry. When at-home genealogy kits became available in 2007, many people were able to trace their own personal genealogy — including the location of family members they may not have known existed.

# Everything to Know About the Fertility Fraud Documentary ‘Our Father’
### Who else is in _Our Father_?
Besides Ballard, _Our Father_ includes insights from Jody Madeira, an Indiana University professor who specializes in reproductive medicine and bioethics. Madeira testified at a 2019 trial for a bill that would’ve made Cline’s abuse a Level 6 felony. Also featured are Angela Ganote, a local Indianapolis news anchor whose initial inquiry led to the criminal investigation into Cline; Tim DeLaney, an Indiana prosecutor; and Dr. Robert Colver, Cline’s onetime medical partner. Several of Cline’s other biological children are also featured in the documentary and speak out about their individual experiences.

# Everything to Know About the Fertility Fraud Documentary ‘Our Father’
### When does _Our Father_ come out?
_Our Father_ will be available to stream on May 11.
